title: Supreme Court Orders New SIT to Probe Ram Mandir Donation Theft as Scandal Deepens
excerpt: Chief Justice Surya Kant directs that a senior IPS officer lead the reconstituted investigation team, saying the probe must be fair and unbiased. The case returns to court on July 27.
body:
• India's Supreme Court ordered the formation of a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT) on Monday, directing that a senior IPS officer lead the probe into alleged theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir.
  • The existing SIT had submitted its status report in a sealed cover on Sunday. The court found the investigation needed to reach a "conclusive stage" and ordered the Solicitor General to bring names for the new team.
  • The alleged theft may exceed ₹5 crore ($600,000), far higher than the ₹80 lakh ($96,000) officially recovered so far. Eight people have been arrested.
  • Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge have demanded an independent investigation and full public disclosure of the trust's accounts.

Court Finds Probe Needs Overhaul

The Supreme Court of India took the unusual step of ordering a completely new investigation team into the Ram Mandir donation theft case on Monday, signalling dissatisfaction with the progress of the existing probe. A three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard four separate petitions related to the scandal and determined that the investigation needed to be escalated.

"A new SIT should be constituted. A senior IPS officer should lead the team so that the investigation can reach a conclusive stage," the CJI said during the 3:30 p.m. hearing. He added that "the probe must be fair and conducted without any bias."

The court directed Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to bring names from the Uttar Pradesh government for the reconstituted SIT, with the next hearing scheduled for July 27.

A Scandal That Keeps Growing

What began as allegations of missing cash from the collection boxes at one of Hinduism's holiest sites has spiralled into a political firestorm that has shaken the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust to its foundations.

The SIT's own findings suggest the total amount siphoned could exceed ₹5 crore — more than six times the ₹80 lakh officially recovered. Investigators believe the trust itself had quietly recovered between ₹2.5 crore and ₹3 crore from the accused before the formal investigation even began, though this has not been officially confirmed. Another ₹2 crore to ₹2.5 crore may have already been spent by the accused.

Eight people have been arrested so far, including temple staff, bank employees, and aides to trust officials. The custodial interrogation of key accused Subhash Srivastava, responsible for counting temple donations, proved decisive — he reportedly admitted to being part of the conspiracy and identified Ramashankar Yadav alias "Tinnu" as the alleged mastermind.

"The credibility of your government and the Trust rests on how transparently and swiftly you act. The people of India are watching."

— Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, in a letter to PM Modi

Political Fallout Intensifies

The scandal has triggered a full-blown political crisis. Congress MP KC Venugopal submitted an Adjournment Motion in the Lok Sabha demanding a parliamentary discussion. The motion alleged systematic financial fraud, citing the destruction of CCTV footage and the removal of a whistleblowing Chief Accounts Officer as evidence of institutional complicity.

Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav described the alleged theft as a "Mahapaap" — a great sin — in Sanatan Dharma and demanded a complete overhaul of the temple trust. He accused the government-appointed SIT of attempting a "whitewash," alleging one of its members faced fraud charges.

The BJP has pushed back sharply, with Uttar Pradesh minister Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary accusing the opposition of politicising a criminal matter. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has repeatedly assured strict action against anyone found guilty.

In a significant intervention, the Nirmohi Akhara — which has historical religious ties to the Ram Janmabhoomi site — moved the Supreme Court seeking to restructure the trust as a public trust, arguing that trustees should be selected from persons of "high integrity" with genuine religious connections. The petition noted that the trust's General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Anil Mishra resigned on July 6 amid the escalating controversy.

Why It Matters to the Diaspora

The Ram Mandir holds deep emotional significance for Hindus worldwide. Many in the diaspora contributed donations to the temple's construction, and the allegations of misappropriation have sparked concern and anger among overseas devotees. The Supreme Court's decision to reconstitute the investigation team may provide some reassurance that accountability will follow, but the case has already damaged trust in the institution charged with managing one of the faith's most sacred sites.

What's Next

The Solicitor General is expected to present names for the new SIT before the July 27 hearing. Meanwhile, the opposition has vowed to press the issue during Parliament's monsoon session. Whether the reconstituted probe can restore public confidence — at home and among the global Hindu diaspora — remains to be seen.
